note: Gameplay settings and small-item placement metadata. The tavern location, furniture, NPCs, spawn markers and transforms are authored in scenes/tavern.tscn.

worlds.note: Select which learning content and small-item staging rule a run uses. Both modes use the same editor-authored tavern location.

tavern.note: The TAV-01 tavern and the playable content of a normal run. Fixed furniture stands where it is authored; only the small things a scenario asks about appear and disappear, each at a station that means something in the room - the prep counter, the guest table, the fridge.

legacy.note: The original LEX-01 practice scenarios and guided beginner flow, retained as regression content. They use candidate-slot staging in the same tavern.

mage.note: Worker: stands at the north wall at the kitchen's east edge, facing west (yaw 90 faces -x) toward the stove and the prep counter. The spot is chosen for the aim lines as much as for the look: the model's pick box is 2.4 x 2.5 m around the node, and every earlier kitchen spot sat inside the walk-and-aim corridor from the entrance to the fridge station, so the crosshair hit the worker instead of the item. Here the box only grazes the stove's box by 0.09 m and the round table's empty corner by 0.35 m, and no spawn-to-station line crosses it.

knight.note: Owner: stands at the south end of the bar run facing north along it. The counters are 2.04 m deep and flush to the west wall, so there is no gap behind the bar; the end of the bar is the spot that reads as the person serving without putting him inside a wall. His weapon-sweep AABB grazes the counter's south end; the body is clear of it and of the south wall.

gast.note: Guest: stands in the gap between guest_table_1 and guest_table_2, facing west toward the first table. The off-centre KayKit bounds remain clear of both table tops.

cameras.note: Scenario contexts select named spawn markers in scenes/tavern.tscn.

player.note: The first-person body and its reach (TAV-02). The player is a capsule on collision layer 1 and the room shell plus the interior entries marked solid are the only things on that layer, so no guest furniture, prop or NPC can block or trap them. interact_range is the only limit on what the crosshair can act on: aiming further away is allowed and is answered with the too-far cue, never with an answer or an attempt.

default_stations.note: Where an object stands when a record names it in the situation but does not say where it is. Authored staging reads a placement slot, never a random position. The default is the kitchen prep counter: a tavern keeps what it serves at the service side, and a bring task then carries it from there to the guest table or to a person, which is what keeps 'bring it to the table' meaningful.

candidate_slots.note: Small-item staging positions for the retained LEX-01 candidate-slot mode, clear of fixed tavern counters. The tavern scenarios use named furniture stations instead.

on_table.note: Item sits on the top surface of the fixed guest table in group 1 (id guest_table_1). The tabletop is measured at y = 1.00; its 1.5 m surface is enough for the few small props in one situation.

on_counter.note: Item stands on the kitchen prep counter - the tavern's keeping place and the station every answer starts at unless the record says otherwise. The anchor is the authored prep counter (id service_counter), its top surface measured at y = 1.00, and it is one of the pieces the player walks into, so an item on it always sits on the far side of a solid piece the player stands in front of.

in_fridge.note: Item stands directly in front of the authored fridge (id kitchen_fridge) and is highlighted. The committed fridge prop has no door, so 'in dem Kuehlschrank' is shown as 'at the fridge' and is stated as a limitation.

hold.note: bring_deliver keeps the picked object on the CarryTraySpawn marker in scenes/tavern.tscn; tray_size controls its visible footprint.

delivery.note: Offset from an NPC origin where a delivered object is placed.
